From: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@openlib.org>

Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: OpenLib - Redwood demo request (GitHub integration)

Hi Camila,

Thanks for the quick startup credits - I just signed up and poked around the API. We're evaluating Redwood because several of our open-source tools on GitHub need to call an LLM for code summarization and CI-time model runs.

Two quick questions before a demo: 1) Do you have an out-of-the-box GitHub Actions integration or a GitHub App? 2) What's the recommended path for running inference from CI without exposing secrets in logs?

Would love a 30-minute demo to walk through integration patterns and pricing for CI bursts. I'm in PDT. Here is our demo-repo: https://github.com/openlib/example-repo

Best,
Sam Taylor
Head of Integrations
OpenLib

Short answers: we have a sample GitHub Actions workflow and a recommended pattern that uses short-lived scoped tokens + prefix (no secrets in CI logs) - happy to show examples. 30 minutes sounds perfect. I can run through the GitHub Actions example, CI best practices, and cost/throughput considerations.

I have availability tomorrow 10:00-12:00 PDT or Wednesday 14:00-16:00 PDT. If neither works feel free to pick a slot on my calendar: https://calendly.com/redwood/camila-30m

Agenda (tentative):
- Quick intro + goals (5m)

I'll loop in our Solutions Engineer for the demo.

Cheers,

Quick note on GitHub Apps: we do support a GitHub App pattern for org-level installs. For CI use cases we often recommend:
- GitHub App for repo-level permissions and install-based auth for service-to-service interactions
- Short-lived tokens for CI jobs with minimal scopes

I've CC'd Jonas (Solutions Engineering) so he can prep a short demo for the example-repo.

See you Wednesday - Camila
